compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Reported in https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/issues/145. A ticket-store remote on S3 can carry
separate fetch and push URLs that name different AWS profiles (a read-only reader for fetch, a
writer for push), set with `git remote set-url --push`. Plain `git push` and `git fetch` work,
because git picks the right URL for each. Several rebar store paths that perform or guard a
WRITE resolve the remote with plain `git remote get-url <remote>`, which returns the FETCH URL.

## Observation (measured in a worktree at origin/main 3b80ff04452, git 2.56.0)

- Reproduced at the `s3remote_factory` seam the existing tests use
  (`tests/integration/s3_doctor_harness.py`): a tracker whose `origin` has fetch URL
  `s3://tickets-reader@bucket/prefix` and push URL `s3://tickets-writer@bucket/prefix`.
  `heal_multi_bundle(tracker, "origin", "tickets", s3remote_factory=recorder)` handed the
  factory `s3://tickets-reader@bucket/prefix`. `git remote get-url --push origin` returned the
  writer URL; with the push URL unset, `--push` returned the fetch URL.
- Read from code: `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:77` resolves the URL with
  `remote get-url`; `_default_factory` (s3_doctor.py:48-54) passes it to
  `git_remote_s3.parse_git_url`, whose `user@` segment becomes the profile, and upstream
  `S3Remote.__init__` (awslabs/git-remote-s3 v0.4.2, `remote.py`) opens
  `boto3.Session(profile_name=profile)`. So the heal's `acquire_lock`, `put_object` and
  `delete_object` run under the reader profile. Not exercised against real S3.
- Measured: a tracker with fetch URL `https://example.invalid/tickets.git`, push URL
  `s3://bucket/tickets` and no git-remote-s3 helper: `push_tickets_branch` returned `None`
  instead of raising `OptionalDependencyError`. The helper preflight at
  `src/rebar/_store/push.py:195` (and the async-arm twin at push.py:124) checks the fetch URL,
  so the fail-closed contract pinned by `tests/integration/test_s3_preflight.py` is skipped
  for a split remote.

## Every remote-URL resolution in the store code, classified

Write paths (URL value is used to authorize or guard a write; fix):
- `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:77` heal_multi_bundle - builds the S3 client that locks,
  writes and deletes. Primary defect.
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py:124` `_require_s3_helper_for_configured_remote` (async push arm).
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py:195` `push_tickets_branch` helper preflight.
- `src/rebar/_commands/completion_delivery.py:628` `deliver_candidate` helper preflight before
  the completion push (same pattern as push.py:195).
- `src/rebar/_commands/_init_probe.py:89` `require_s3_helper_if_s3_remote` (init/mount): the
  mounted store both fetches and pushes, so it must check the fetch URL AND the push URL.

Not write paths (no change):
- `src/rebar/_store/footprint.py:274` - URL used for a temporary `git clone` (a read).
- `src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:268-275` - compares the code repo's and tracker's fetch URLs
  to decide freshness reporting (read-side).
- Existence-only probes that discard the URL: `_lib_ops.py:294`, `reconciler/last_pass.py:76`,
  `reconciler/_advisory_lock.py:72` (via `git_adapter.remote_get_url`),
  `_commands/fsck_tracker_health.py:181`, `_commands/_init_probe.py:84`. `git remote get-url`
  fails for a missing remote with or without `--push`, so the answer is unchanged.

## Approach

Resolve the URL with `git remote get-url --push <remote>` at the four write-path sites
(s3_doctor.py:77, push.py:124, push.py:195, completion_delivery.py:628). That is the URL
`git push` itself uses, and git falls back to the fetch URL when no push URL is configured
(measured above), so single-URL remotes behave exactly as today. In `_init_probe.py`
`require_s3_helper_if_s3_remote`, run the helper check for both the fetch and the push URL.
Inline flag changes; no new helper, config key or mechanism. Out of scope: real-S3 or AWS
resources; files under concurrent edit elsewhere (`reducer/_api.py`, `_engine_support/reads.py`,
`validate.py`, `graph/_loader.py`, `gates.py`, `reducer/_inbound.py`, `bridge_fsck_drift.py`)
are not touched.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py`
- `src/rebar/_store/push.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/completion_delivery.py`
- `src/rebar/_commands/_init_probe.py`
- `tests/integration/test_s3_doctor.py`
- `tests/integration/test_s3_preflight.py`
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py`
- `tests/unit/test_sync_remote_config.py` (its exact-argument assertion on the push guard gains `--push`)

## Testing

Failing tests first, each confirmed red on origin/main before the fix:
- `test_s3_doctor.py`: split remote (reader fetch URL, writer push URL) - the recording
  factory receives the writer URL and the heal completes; plus a no-push-URL case where the
  factory receives the single configured URL (unchanged behaviour).
- `test_s3_preflight.py`: split-scheme remote (https fetch, s3 push), helper absent -
  `push_tickets_branch` (sync arm) and the async arm raise `OptionalDependencyError`;
  `init._mount_or_create_branch` raises it as well. Edge: s3 fetch URL with a non-s3 push URL
  still fails closed at init (the store fetches from S3).
- `test_atomic_completion_close.py`: tracker remote with a bare-repo fetch URL
  (`init_bare_remote`) and an `s3://` push URL, helper absent - completion delivery raises
  `CommandError` "completion delivery preflight failed".
Then `pytest -m integration` on test_s3_doctor.py, test_s3_doctor_heldout.py,
test_s3_preflight.py, and `make verify`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `heal_multi_bundle` builds its S3 client from the push URL: the new split-remote test in
  `tests/integration/test_s3_doctor.py` passes and fails on origin/main.
- [ ] A remote with no push URL still heals with its single URL (new no-push-URL test passes;
  existing `test_s3_doctor.py` and `test_s3_doctor_heldout.py` stay green).
- [ ] The sync and async push helper preflights check the push URL: new split-scheme tests in
  `test_s3_preflight.py` raise `OptionalDependencyError`, and fail on origin/main.
- [ ] Completion delivery's preflight checks the push URL: the new test in
  `test_atomic_completion_close.py` raises "completion delivery preflight failed".
- [ ] Init/mount checks both fetch and push URLs: the new init tests in `test_s3_preflight.py`
  pass.
- [ ] `make verify` passes (apart from the host's known pandoc-architecture reconciler
  failures, compared by name), and the S3 integration files above pass under `-m integration`.
- [ ] The change lands on main through Gerrit with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

## File impact

The eight paths listed under Scope, recorded with `rebar set-file-impact`.
